content.heading: My Education: Work Harder than Everyone Else
paragraphs: You constantly hear about amazing people who dropped out of College. I went one further. I dropped out of High School. In reality I was kicked out as much as I decided to leave.

content.heading: School of Hard Knocks
paragraphs: I was brought to the USA illegally as a baby and I my parents made the choice that our house would be more American than the people who lived next door. My parents only whispered in spanish to each other, but to me, it was English only.

When I was 13 my mother died of cancer and my father left us and moved back to Mexico while she was ill. When she died, I was left to fend for myself in east LA. I had grown up in San Diego, and East LA was a totally different world.

content.heading: The Public Library: My University and Sancutary
paragraphs: In order to escape the drugs and gangs and the heat, I retreated to the library, where I found world of books and computers, and in a way, I found my home. As these computers were hooked up to the early internet, I had access to just about anything I wanted to learn.

I was reading books on Unix and C, and I was playing games on public BBS servers and discovering a love for programming and web development. Angelfire, and Geocities was my playground and I loved making horrid, ugly web pages that detailed my passions.

In trying to find a way to break the Windows95 protections, so I could build C (and Delphi) programs. It was a slow process and I think it would have been frustrating to most people, but to me, it was the ultimate adventure!

Once I had broken the security and installed compilers for C and Delphi, I dug my heels in and spent every hour the library was open, learning and making mistakes, and searching the hour for hours on end.

content.heading: A Skateboard for a Car, and Pounding the Pavement
paragraphs: Armed with my new skills in HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, I went door to door - cyber cafes, pizza joints, and even a water filtration store run out of a guy's garage, I pitched ways I could increase business by building websites and Windows software. I demonstrated how I could help businesses set up networks and secure their computers from viruses and unauthorized access.

I got at least 50 hard 'No' responses before I got a maybe or even a 'Yes', but they did happen, and at 16 I could start affording a motel room. It was dirty, and most of the residents were drug addicts or sex workers, but I was finally inside and I had my own key. At this point I was unstoppable, and I think it shaped me into the guided missile I am to this day. You point me at something impossible, and I will always find a way to make it happen.

content.heading: Recruiters: My Secret Weapon
paragraphs: I looked up every recruiting company in the greater LA area and made a list and started visiting one after the other. I didnt know what a 'real' resume was supposed to look like, so I was putting a web based resume on CD Roms I would make while grinding it out at CompUSA where I was paid minimum wage to fix computers. I didnt have a phone of my own, so I was accepting calls from recruiters on the CompUSA phone. Eventually I was warned to the point of being fired, but then it happened. I got placed at Intel. The only problem was, I was in southern California, and the job was in Oregon.

With only a skateboard for transportation, I started asking around with my street friends, looking for options. I discovered two things. Hitch-hiking and train riding. And I did copious amounts of both. And I arrived in the cold, wet north for my first day of work. I was tired, and I only had 1 set of work clothes. (black tie, white shirt, khaki slacks)

My education had only started, and I spent all my spare time reading programming books. The one problem. I couldnt afford the cost of these books (Wrox Press for instance), so I bought a single book at Barnes and Nobles and when I had taken all my notes, and had stayed late at work to go through all the book, I would return it for store credit, and get the next book. C++, C, JavaScript, Perl, and later ASP.Net - this is how I funded my education.
I learned everything I could from the 'old guys' at work, and I worked through lunch and stayed late every night. I even slept in the bathroom more than a few times due to the cold and rain.

content.heading: The Trip back to California
paragraphs: I can't tell you how happy I was to get back to California and get out of the rain. After a couple of years of it, I had reached my limit. I now had an apartment, and some clothes, and recruiters were calling my phone and emailing me more and more. So when I got the call to work at UpperDeck I was elated beyond words. I spent my last paycheck to buy a real clunker of a car (a volkswagen bug) and I packed up my few belongings and I headed back 'home', to sunny San Diego.

My education was just getting started. I kept learning from older devs, and I kept staying late very day and working through weekends. I kept building crappy computers out of second hand parts and wrigin in every programming language I could get a book on. I came from nothing, but I was not nothing. I was shaping up as a hell of a programmer. Not because I had a CS degree (which I didnt and dont) but because I woutworked everyone, especially my Bosses.
